start_here: Say to your AI: "Turn my agent skills into workflows. My private words are Acme Corp and Project Falcon. Do a dry run first." It runs tool:turn-my-agent-skills-into-workflows on the skills in your agent-skills list and tells you which skills would become workflows and which stay home, and why.

lists.label: Agent skills
lists.holds: One row per file of each agent skill folder you have installed (a long file is several rows, in parts). A skill is a folder holding a SKILL.md with a name and a description. (The rows keep these as file.path, file.folder and document.text.)

lists.label: Workflows
lists.holds: One row per workflow in your own account: its id, title, what it is for, and (as text) its input, source and files. Each has step rows (record:workflow-step) holding what the AI does.

instructions: 1. Make sure your agent-skills list holds your installed skills (each file of each skill folder is a record:agent-skill row).
2. Say "Turn my agent skills into workflows, dry run first", with any words that name your private people, businesses or systems in private_words.

3. Read what comes back: made (the workflows that would be written), home (each skill left out, with the kind of reason: a secret key, a folder on your computer, an email address, a phone number or a private word) and stale (workflows of earlier runs whose skill is gone).

4. Fix or remove what a left-out skill names, then say it again without dry_run: each clean skill is written as workflow: then skill- then the skill's name in your own account, with its text files under files.
5. Run one: say "Run the id it was written under" with what you want done in request; the AI starts it with tool:start-a-recipe-run.

worked_examples.title: A dry run keeps the skill that names a computer folder at home
worked_examples.ask: Turn my agent skills into workflows, dry run first.
worked_examples.given: Two skills in your list: tidy-notes (clean) and open-folder, whose SKILL.md says to open a folder under ~/Documents.
worked_examples.hands_back: made: ["workflow:skill-tidy-notes"], home: [{ skill: "open-folder", reasons: ["SKILL.md names a folder on one person's computer"] }], written: 0. The text that matched is never printed.

worked_examples.title: Run the workflow a skill became

input.request: Tidy my three notes about the garden.

worked_examples.given: workflow:skill-tidy-notes was written by an earlier run.
worked_examples.hands_back: A job for your AI whose one step, follow-the-skill, holds the skill's instructions and lists its files (template.md) to read from the workflow's files.

pour.how: Name the list of workflows you already keep and its fields. The tool matches each kit field to one of yours (by the map you give, the same id, the same label, or a name in alike), refuses when fewer than least_coverage of the kit's fields match, and otherwise answers the records:write that adds the example rows to your list, leaving your own rows untouched.
